title: T is for TRIM: Stop fighting your flight controls! | MSFS A-Z
description:
That frustrating "roller coaster" flight path isn't a bad joystick—it's a lack of trim. Welcome back to our Microsoft Flight Simulator A-Z series! Today, we’ve reached the letter T, and we are tackling the ultimate secret to smooth, relaxed, and professional flight: Aerodynamic Trim.

Many beginners think the trim wheel is used to steer or change pitch. That is a myth that leads to constant overcorrection and pilot-induced oscillations. In this episode, we break down the physics of trim tabs, why an aircraft trims for speed rather than an angle, and how to transition from aggressively wrestling your aircraft to flying it with absolute precision.

In this video, you’ll discover:
- The core physics: How a tiny trim tab holds a massive elevator in place.
- The golden rule: A step-by-step guide to the "Pitch, Hold, Trim" technique.
- The power & flap trap: Why changing your throttle makes the nose balloon or plunge.
- Boeing vs. Airbus: How commercial airliner trim systems completely flip the philosophy.

🕒 Chapters
00:00 - Intro: The cramping wrist problem
00:45 - The theory: What is aerodynamic trim?
01:30 - Pro-tip: The golden rule (Pitch, Hold, Trim)
02:15 - Demo: Takeoff & climb stability adjustments
04:40 - The secret: Trimming for speed, not attitude
05:20 - Demo: Final approach & flap management
06:50 - Advanced tech: Boeing manual switches vs. Airbus Fly-By-Wire

Whether you are a real-world student pilot trying to stabilize your climb or a desktop simmer looking to nail manual instrument approaches without autopilot, mastering the trim wheel is what makes you a safer, smoother pilot.
